verses.text: [This section in some manuscripts appears in chapter 15]
Mordecai prepared the letters, and sealed them with the king's ring.
These letters were sent by couriers throughout all the provinces.
The king permitted the Jews in every city to gather and defend their lives.
They were to destroy any armed force that might attack them, with their children and women.
And they were allowed to take their plunder.
On one day throughout all the provinces of King Artaxerxes:
on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar.

The following is a copy of this letter: [br]"The Great King, Artaxerxes, to the governors of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, and to those who are loyal to our government, greetings.

[vbr]Many people, the more they are honored with the most generous kindness of their benefactors, the more proud they become, and not only seek to harm our subjects, but, in their inability to bear prosperity, they even try to scheme against their own benefactors. They not only fail to show gratitude, but, swept away by the boasting of those ignorant of goodness, they assume they will escape the justice of God, who always sees everything. Often, many set in authority have, by the persuasion of friends entrusted with public affairs, been in part responsible for the shedding of innocent blood and become involved in irreparable calamities, when those persons by false trickery of their evil natures deceive the sincere goodwill of their sovereigns.

What has been wickedly accomplished through the corrupt behavior of those who unworthily exercise authority can be seen from considering recent matters, more than from the ancient records. In the future, we will take care to render our kingdom quiet and peaceful for all by changing our methods and always judging what comes before our eyes with greater fairness.
For Haman son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian, an alien far from Persian blood and devoid of our kindness, having become our guest,
enjoyed so fully the goodwill we show to every nation that he was called our father and was continually honored by all as second to the royal throne.

But, unable to restrain his pride, he plotted to take away our life and kingdom, and with cunning and deceit sought the destruction of Mordecai, our savior and perpetual benefactor, and Esther, the blameless partner of our kingdom, together with their entire nation.
He thought that by these means he would catch us undefended and transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.

But we find that the Jews, who were doomed to annihilation by this most evil man, are not criminals, but are governed by just laws and are children of the living God, most high, most mighty, who has guided the kingdom for us and for our ancestors in the best order.

Therefore, you will do well not to carry out the letters sent by Haman son of Hammedatha, since he who did these things has been hanged at the gate of Susa with all his household—for God, who rules over all things, quickly repaid him with the punishment he deserved.
Therefore, publicly post a copy of this letter in every place and allow the Jews to live under their own laws.
Give them support, so that on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month—Adar—that very day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them at the time of oppression.
For God, who rules over all, has turned this day for his chosen people from destruction into joy.

Therefore, keep this day joyfully among your commemorative festivals, so that both now and hereafter it may represent deliverance for you and the loyal Persians, but a reminder of destruction for those who plot against us.

Every city and country, without exception, that does not act accordingly shall be destroyed in wrath with spear and fire, and be made not only impassable for humans, but also forever hateful to wild animals and birds."
